rules: Four of sixteen rejects this round came from one mechanical pattern: swapping only the numerator field (return, close-open, high-open, high-close) inside TS_MEAN(numerator / ($dollar_volume + eps), ~10 days) while holding the denominator and window fixed. This keeps rho at 0.86-0.97 against each other or a plain dollar-volume mean, and the same guarded-denominator subtree also trips archive_subtree elsewhere. Treat this ratio family as exhausted; a new candidate needs a different denominator construction, not a different numerator.

Inside CS_RANK(fundamental) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63), both $earnings_per_share (rho 0.804) and price-scaled $roe (rho 0.895) collapsed back onto the archived $roe version. EPS now behaves like a member of the ROA/ROE profitability cluster for correlation purposes, and dividing by $close does not escape it. $asset_turnover on the same leg stayed independent and accepted (2.016); vary the accounting dimension, not the profitability field or its price-scaling.

A dollar-volume-normalized intraday-move ratio and a stochastic-style range-position ratio shared no operators, fields, or windows yet hit rho 0.859. Passing archive_subtree is not evidence a candidate will clear correlation; weigh what real-world signal a new shape approximates against archive members that answer something similar, not just ones that look similar on paper.

Bare CS_RANK/RANK of $earnings_per_share and $book_per_share (no TS_* window, no delta) cleared coverage cleanly, including the round's best fitness (6.794) and two more accepts. Coverage risk for these fields is specific to windowing or differencing them, not to using the level; don't discount an EPS- or book-per-share-anchored proposal on coverage grounds unless it is also windowed.

TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21)) accepted at 4.998 with no fundamental leg at all, the round's second-best. The winning assignment put TS_RANK on the leg that varies within a name over time and CS_RANK on a cross-sectional dispersion stat of the other leg; don't default to requiring a fundamental partner in every price/volume product.

TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, 21), 21) accepted at 4.507. Rank-transforming the volume leg is what rescues a return/volume correlation; raw-return-vs-raw-volume stays a dead end, but the fix is TS_RANK on volume, not abandoning the pairing.

The fundamental-minus-raw-leg rank spread set a new round-best (6.794, EPS minus a bounded price-position ratio); keep exploring bounded price ratios as the 'other' leg, not just volume/range ranks. The one spread that failed did so on coverage from a 252-day window on the non-fundamental leg, not the fundamental choice; cap any window in a spread at 63 days regardless of which leg carries it.

Two crossover children were rejected for donating only 2 shared nodes from a normal 5-node parent instead of exactly 3, both against the same RANK($roa) * RANK($dollar_volume) parent, both replacing one whole branch and keeping only the other operator-plus-leaf pair. Target an exactly-3-node shared subtree with each parent, not a whole branch or a single leaf.
